provider_query: CPython source file that defines PyObject_Malloc
answer:
**`Objects/obmalloc.c`** defines `PyObject_Malloc` in CPython (main and older branches).

1. **Definition** — `Objects/obmalloc.c` implements `void *PyObject_Malloc(size_t size)`, which rejects sizes above `PY_SSIZE_T_MAX` and dispatches to the object-domain allocator (`_PyObject.malloc`).  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Objects/obmalloc.c

2. **Pymalloc backend** — Same file defines `_PyObject_Malloc` (used when `WITH_PYMALLOC` is on), which tries the small-block allocator then falls back to the raw allocator.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Objects/obmalloc.c

3. **Declaration** — `Include/objimpl.h` declares `PyAPI_FUNC(void *) PyObject_Malloc(size_t size)` and the `PyObject_MALLOC` alias.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Include/objimpl.h

4. **3.7 definition** — Same public function in `Objects/obmalloc.c` on the 3.7 branch.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.7/Objects/obmalloc.c

5. **2.7 definition** — Older direct pymalloc entry point `#undef PyObject_Malloc` / `PyObject_Malloc` in `Objects/obmalloc.c`.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/2.7/Objects/obmalloc.c

6. **Docs** — `Doc/c-api/memory.rst` lists `PyObject_Malloc` under `PYMEM_DOMAIN_OBJ` and pymalloc.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/c-api/memory.rst

7. **Related docs** — `Doc/c-api/allocation.rst` notes `PyObject_New` allocates via `PyObject_Malloc`.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/c-api/allocation.rst

8. **Free-threaded path** — `Include/internal/pycore_object_alloc.h` selects a mimalloc heap, then calls `PyObject_Malloc`.  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Include/internal/pycore_object_alloc.h

results.snippet:
Using inheritance in an object oriented language requires us to define a parent class with all the common attributes and behaviors that should be inherited by all of its child classes. To achieve the same effect in C, we need to define a parent struct which contains all the common attributes.

This is where the `PyObject` struct comes into the picture. CPython defines a struct called `PyObject` for this purpose. It is defined in the file Include/object.h, and shown in the following figure. [...] Definition of the `PyObject` struct in CPython [...] By embedding the `PyObject` struct as the first field in every object’s definition, CPython ensures that their in-memory representation starts with a common header which is formed by the `PyObject` itself.
